Title: SQL Injection in customer export endpoint
Technical Impact: Severity of PII extraction and data integrity destruction in the payments database.
Business Impact: Regulatory exposure under GDPR and PCI DSS; potential brand and revenue impact.
Remediation: Migrate all queries to parameterized statements; apply strict allow-list validation on all date inputs; add WAF rules and run DAST in CI.
Evidence: Boolean-based blind injection returned 200 with row count 1 when payload IF(1=1,...)

Title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) on invoice endpoint
Technical Impact: Unauthorized disclosure of financial records for any account.
Business Impact: Customer data leakage; reputational and legal risk.
Remediation: Enforce ownership-based authorization checks on every object reference; consider randomized identifiers and signed references.
Evidence: Sequential ID enumeration returned invoices for 40+ unrelated accounts without authentication errors.

Title: SSRF via PDF generator allows internal network scanning
Technical Impact: Internal network reconnaissance and access to cloud metadata (IMDS) with temporary credentials.
Business Impact: Lateral movement enabler; potential compromise of internal services and secrets.
Remediation: Restrict outbound traffic from generator service, block link-local/metadata ranges, allow-list trusted hosts, and adopt URL schema validation.
Evidence: Request to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ returned IAM role name for the service account.

Title: Weak TLS cipher suites on corporate VPN
Technical Impact: Captured VPN handshakes can be downgraded/decrypted, exposing session material.
Business Impact: Credential and session exposure for remote workforce.
Remediation: Disable TLS < 1.2, remove export/weak cipher suites (e.g., CBC, RC4, 3DES), enforce certificate pinning policies.
Evidence: TLS scan reported 14 insecure cipher suites including TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.

Title: Privileged access via default admin token in developer console
Technical Impact: Full administrative control of identity platform datasets and delegated authentication flows.
Business Impact: Complete compromise of identity and access management; supply-chain risk to all downstream applications.
Remediation: Rotate tokens, disable default credentials, enforce MFA + conditional access on the console, and review privileged role assignments.
Evidence: Documented default token accepted and issued cloud-admin scoped session.

Title: Outdated third-party library with known RCE (Apache Log4j core)
Technical Impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on the scheduler host.
Business Impact: Ransomware and data-exfiltration staging point on payment path.
Remediation: Upgrade Log4j to >= 2.17.1 or 3.x; add SCA scanning to CI; inventory all Java runtimes; verify no JNDI sinks remain.
Evidence: Chained ${jndi:ldap://...} payload triggered outbound LDAP callback from scheduler host.

Title: Security events not logged for failed administrative logins
Technical Impact: Brute-force and credential-stuffing campaigns against admin accounts are invisible to security teams.
Business Impact: Delayed detection of account takeover; compliance gaps in audit proof.
Remediation: Emit structured audit events for all auth failures, ship them to SIEM, tune alert rules, and test detection scenarios.
Evidence: 1,200 failed admin logins over 72h produced zero alerts and zero events in SIEM search.

Title: Unused services exposed on public firewall rules
Technical Impact: Expanded attack surface; SNMP default community strings readable.
Business Impact: Unauthorized reconnaissance and abuse of legacy features.
Remediation: Apply least functionality: close 21/161, remove admin panel from the internet, and centralize change reviews for firewall rules.
Evidence: External scan enumerated FTP banner of internal build server (reveals hostname).

Title: Missing rate limiting on password reset allows MFA bypass
Technical Impact: Account takeover of any user with a single reset code brute force.
Business Impact: Widespread account compromise; regulatory notification obligations.
Remediation: Rate limit reset attempts, use short-lived high-entropy tokens, bind reset to session, require re-authentication for critical actions, and monitor anomalous reset flows.
Evidence: 6-digit code brute-forced within 2 hours using distributed request pattern without trigger of WAF or SIEM rules.
